steps.tx: The **dynamic hip screw** serves as the gold-standard extramedullary fixation construct for stable intertrochanteric extracapsular femoral fractures. The device comprises a large-diameter lag screw that slides freely within a side barrel attached to a lateral cortical plate. This geometry allows controlled impaction of fracture fragments along the femoral neck axis during postoperative physiological weight-bearing.
steps.say: The dynamic hip screw is the gold standard implant for stable intertrochanteric hip fractures. It pairs a stout lag screw sliding inside a side barrel plate. As the patient bears weight, the screw slides smoothly down the barrel, compacting the fracture ends together and promoting rapid bone union.

vis.title: DHS Components and Biomechanics
rows: Purchases dense cancellous bone in femoral head
Secures construct to lateral femoral cortex

steps.tx: The biomechanical cornerstone of successful fixation is the **tip-apex distance**, formulated by Baumgaertner in 1995. It is calculated by summing the distance in millimeters from the tip of the lag screw to the apex of the femoral head on anteroposterior and lateral radiographs. A tip-apex distance less than twenty-five millimeters is mandatory to minimize lag screw cut-out through the femoral head.
steps.say: Baumgaertner tip-apex distance is the single most important predictor of DHS success. Add the distance from the screw tip to the femoral head apex on both the AP and lateral views. This sum must remain under twenty-five millimeters. If it exceeds twenty-five millimeters, the screw is at high risk of cutting out.

left.title: Safe Tip-Apex Distance
points: Screw placed central or inferior on AP
Screw placed dead central on lateral view
Lag screw cut-out rate under 1 percent

right.title: Unsafe Tip-Apex Distance
points: Thin purchase in soft osteoporotic bone

steps.tx: A catastrophic mechanical failure is **screw cut-out**, where the lag screw extrudes superiorly through the femoral head cartilage into the hip joint. Cut-out results from inadequate bone mineral density, poor reduction with varus collapse, and excessive tip-apex distance. To avoid cut-out, the surgeon must place the screw centrally or slightly inferior on the frontal projection and precisely central on lateral fluoroscopy.
steps.say: Screw cut-out is a disastrous failure where the metal screw cuts through the top of the femoral head into the joint. It happens when bones are osteoporotic, the neck collapses into varus, or the screw is placed too far from the apex. Always seat the screw deep and central to eliminate cut-out risk.

vis.title: Risk Factors for Fixation Failure
rows: Seat screw within 10 mm of joint line

steps.tx: A critical **biomechanical contraindication** to the dynamic hip screw is an unstable fracture pattern featuring lateral wall incompetence or reverse obliquity (AO/OTA 31-A3). In reverse obliquity fractures, the fracture line runs obliquely downward and laterally. Sliding along the lag screw causes paradoxical lateral shaft displacement and fixation blowout, demanding a cephalomedullary intramedullary nail instead.
steps.say: Never use a dynamic hip screw for reverse obliquity intertrochanteric fractures. Because the fracture line angles downward and outward, sliding down the barrel pushes the shaft outward into catastrophic collapse. Reverse obliquity fractures and blown lateral walls require an intramedullary nail.

right.title: Intramedullary Nail Indication
points: Broken or thin lateral wall (<20 mm)
High bending load requires intramedullary buttress

steps.tx: Postoperative management encourages early **weight-bearing mobilization** on post-op day one, minimizing recumbency-related mortality from pneumonia, pressure ulcers, and deep venous thrombosis. Dynamic sliding transfers compressive forces directly across the intact medial calcar femorale. Patients achieve stable radiographic bone union within eight to twelve weeks, with hardware removal rarely indicated unless lateral trochanteric bursal irritation develops.
steps.say: Get patients out of bed and weight-bearing on post-op day one. Early mobilization slashes mortality from pneumonia, blood clots, and bedsores. The sliding screw transfers weight safely across the fracture line, allowing the bone to knit firmly within eight to twelve weeks.

vis.title: Postoperative Protocol and Timelines
rows: Quad strengthening and hip abductor retraining

quiz.q: What is the maximum safe threshold for tip-apex distance (TAD) in dynamic hip screw fixation?
quiz.explain: Baumgaertner established that a total tip-apex distance (TAD) under 25 mm on AP and lateral radiographs significantly reduces the risk of lag screw cut-out to under 1 percent.

quiz.q: Which fracture pattern represents a contraindication to dynamic hip screw fixation?
options: Intertrochanteric fracture with intact lateral wall
quiz.explain: Reverse obliquity fractures have an inverted fracture plane where telescoping along the DHS lag screw causes lateral shaft translation and mechanical collapse. A cephalomedullary nail is indicated.
